# Factory Functions

A reusable function library for constructing child documents from configured templates, recording creation intent, assigning identities, and preparing participant, access and source connections. It also inherits functions for source binding, access registration, activation and amendment proposals. Creation triggers and caller authorization belong to the integrating clause; the existence of these functions does not itself authorize a caller.

Document paths refer to the document executing a function. Paths within a `child` or `prepared` argument refer to that child document.

## Configuration and creation

`configurationParameters` reads `parameters` from `connectionConfiguration`, defaulting to `{}`. `connectionConfiguration` and `connectionSnapshots` are integration hooks. `configuredTemplate` selects `parameters.template` when present, otherwise `connectionSnapshots.template`. `configuredTemplateValue(path)` reads the corresponding document value beneath `/clauses/<clauseKey>/parameters/template` or the location supplied by `bindings.template`.

`checkCreation(input)` requires `key` to be nonempty text containing neither `/` nor `~`. The destination is the `key` entry beneath `bindings.collection`; no collection default is supplied.

The recorded `creationIntent` contains:

- `templateBlueId`: the identity of the configured template.
- `partyBindings`: `bindings.parties`, defaulting to `{}`.
- `inheritChannels`: the configured channel list, defaulting to `[]`.
- `sourcePaths`: the configured legacy source mapping, defaulting to `{}`.
- `fields` and `values`: input maps, each defaulting to `{}`.
- `requestId`: the supplied value, defaulting to `key`.

If the destination exists, its `creationIntent` must equal this intent exactly. A match returns `outcome: duplicate`, `key` and `path`; a mismatch rejects with `DOCUMENT_KEY_CONFLICT`. Duplicate detection compares these recorded fields. An unused destination returns `outcome: acceptedNew`, `key`, `path` and `intent`, without constructing or writing a document.

`constructDocument(checked, input)` builds the child and runs construction guards. `create(checked, input)` calls it, appends an `add` change at `checked.path`, and emits an event with `kind: Document Started`, `clause: clauseKey`, `entityId: key` and `path`. It returns `acceptedNew`, `key` and `path`. It does not call `checkCreation` or `configureSources`; callers must sequence those separately where needed. Neither the preliminary `acceptedNew` nor the creation event establishes child initialization, activation, consent or external completion.

## Child preparation and customization

The template must have no `/contracts/initialized` entry.

When `bindings.parties` is nonempty, construction uses `prepareChild`. The child must declare the required activation clause. Mappings associate declared child roles with either a role in the executing document's `/activation/parties` or an explicit Party value. Every declared role needs a mapping unless listed in `suppliedParties`, which defaults to `[]`; supplied roles must be declared and unmapped, and retain their declarations. Unknown mappings are rejected.

Mapped parties must satisfy their declarations and have a lead channel plus a nonempty list of unique, nonempty text `readerKeys`. Main-party identity comparisons require the same lead channel and the same reader-key set. Every configuring parent party must remain represented among the resolved child parties. Preparation preserves existing child access paths, adds references to parent access publications under `/timelineAccess/configurer…`, and installs resolved participant channels. Conflicting access locations or different existing channels are rejected. Mapping identities does not grant access or consent.

Without explicit party mappings, construction calls `activateChild` with `frozen: false`. If the executing document has no `/activation`, that helper returns the child unchanged. Otherwise, configured `parties` selects parent roles; its default empty list selects all parent parties. `readers`, defaulting to `[]`, selects named parent readers. Selected names must exist. The helper copies parent access references under `/timelineAccess/grant…`, configures the child's activation parties, readers and access paths, preserves its `required` list or defaults that list to `[]`, and installs participant transports.

Additional customization follows these rules:

- `inheritChannels` copies explicitly permitted participant channels from `/contracts/<role>`. Names must be nonempty text without `/` or `~`; a different channel already present in the child is rejected.
- `fields` assigns top-level values only for names included in `allowedFields`. Even when allowlisted, these names are forbidden: `contracts`, `clauses`, `type`, `itemType`, `keyType`, `valueType`, `value`, `items`, `blueId`, `blue`, `schema`, `constraints`, `mergePolicy`, `properties`, `$previous`, `$previousItems`, `$pos`, `$replace`, `$empty`, and `instanceKey`.
- `values` assigns named values through `fieldPaths`, whose default is `{}`. Each name must resolve to a text path beginning with `/` and an existing child slot. The first path segment cannot be empty or be `contracts`, `clauses`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `sources`, `type`, `blueId`, `instanceKey`, `creationIntent`, or `preparationContext`. Each supplied value is validated against the slot's existing constraint before assignment.
- Legacy `sourcePaths` maps source names to paths in the executing document. Each selected source must have `/contracts/initialized`; its publication reference is included in the child's `sources`.

Construction records `creationIntent` and derives `instanceKey` from the executing document's initialized original, `clauseKey` and `key`. `/clauseRuntime/initialDocument` supplies the original when `/contracts/initialized/document` is absent. Each configured `identityChildren` path must select an existing, uninitialized child template; its `instanceKey` incorporates the enclosing identity and that path.

## Access and named-source configuration

`configureSources(checked, prepared)` first calls `configureDocumentAccess`. That helper reserves `/clauses/documentAccess` and rejects an existing clause there. It creates a `registerAccess_<role>` workflow binding for each party in the prepared activation parameters. Each request contains `documents`: one to sixteen existing, initialized Timeline Access publications.

Named sources use `bindings.sources`. Nonempty named mappings cannot coexist with nonempty legacy `sourcePaths`. Mappings must exactly cover the declarations returned by `configuredSources`; aliases must pass `validPartyName`. Each binding must be text: `self` selects the executing document, while other strings select document paths. A selected source must have an initialized original, have `/activation/active` exactly `true`, and pass `sourceDeclarationMatches`.

`configuredSources` and `sourceDeclarationMatches` have bodies that reject with `SOURCE_VALIDATOR_NOT_COMPILED`; source configuration requires configured implementations of these hooks.

For each named source, preparation records a requirement containing `declaration`, immutable process `origin`, and `selectionPath`. For `self`, `selectionPath` is `checked.path`; otherwise it is empty. With nonempty mappings, `/clauses/documentSources` is reserved, the prepared `/sources` is set to `{}`, and a Source Binding Clause is installed with those requirements and a `bindSource_<role>` workflow binding for each prepared party. This prepares requirements without binding the source publications. With no mappings, the helper returns after access-clause preparation and declaration-count checking.

## Source binding and readiness

Inherited `bindSource` accepts a declared `alias` and an existing source publication in `document`. A nonempty `sourcePath` overrides `document`. Validation requires the configured process origin, active state exactly `true`, and coverage of every executing-document party by matching lead-channel and reader-key identity; role names need not match.

A new binding adds a publication reference at `/sources/<alias>` and returns `acceptedNew`. After validating the candidate, an existing binding with the required origin returns `duplicate` without replacing its publication. A different existing origin is rejected as `SOURCE_REBINDING_FORBIDDEN`.

`namedSourcesReady` requires every declared source to be initialized, retain its configured origin, be active, and cover the document's party roster. A nonempty `selectionPath` must additionally select an initialized document within that source whose process origin matches the executing document. With no requirements, the function returns `true`.

`refreshSourceReadiness` records the result at `/sourceLinks/ready` and emits an event carrying `ready` when it changes. Its `acceptedNew` result does not imply that readiness became true or changed. The installed Source Binding Clause refreshes once on initialization, on `/activation` or `/sources` changes, and on source collection advancement. An absent `/sourceLinks/ready` is unknown. Source readiness does not replace commercial approval requirements.

## Access registration

Inherited `registerDocumentAccess` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be `true` and `call/channel` to identify a party in `/activation/parties`. `installTimelineAccess` requires one to sixteen `documents` and uses the caller-supplied `basePath`; no base-path default is established.

Each publication must be a Timeline Access document with the required provider channel, an initialized original and provider checkpoint history. Its original and current executable contracts must match the prescribed provider-and-update policy, allowing the current initialization and checkpoint records.

Publications are registered by original process identity. Already-known identities are not replaced; an entirely duplicate batch returns `duplicate`. New registrations add publication references, embedded access-event channels and activation refresh handlers, and extend `/activation/registeredAccessChannels` and `/activation/accessPaths`. Registration preserves provider ownership of permission changes. Usable participant access is evaluated separately through `accessValid`; registering a publication is not confirmation of a new provider grant.

## Inherited activation and participant operations

Activation distinguishes access readiness from acceptance. `computeState` derives `accessReady` and `functional` through `accessValid`, including additions in access requests whose `expectedRevision` matches the current revision. `termsAccepted` requires every role in `required` to be approved and `termsCurrent` to succeed. `active` additionally requires valid access and a document that is not closed.

Computed `status` is `CLOSED`, `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`, or `ACTIVE`, according to closure, access, previous activation and acceptance. `everActivated` records whether activation has occurred. Missing stored state is not an inferred status or approval. The detailed access and current-terms policies are delegated to their respective checks.

`approve` requires exact document review, a party caller, the current `revision`, and valid participant access. `termsRef` is required when `negotiation.allowedPaths` is nonempty; whenever supplied, it must equal `/activation/terms/ref`. A repeated approval returns without adding another approval event. A new approval records that party's acceptance and commits activation state; a successful return does not mean all required parties have approved. If this activates the document, a pending negotiation proposal is recorded as `SUPERSEDED` and negotiation becomes noneditable.

`initializeTerms` retains existing terms. Otherwise it builds a reviewed terms identity from the initial definition and configured scalar negotiation fields, excluding access publications, reader configuration and party reader keys. It initializes `termsRevision` and `negotiation.revision` to `1`, with an editable negotiation and empty proposal, history and outcomes.

`updateParty` requires exact review, an unfrozen roster and a party caller. `party` defaults to the caller's role. Existing roles can only be changed by their own caller; adding a role requires `allowNewParties`. `replacement` must include `lead.channel`, names must pass validation, and the resulting roster must have valid access. Success updates participant contracts, clears approvals and advances the revision; a newly added role is appended to `required`.

`admitApprovedParties` requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, a nonempty configured `admission.approvers` policy, valid main-party identities and usable access. Existing roles must retain their main identity. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; a changed roster updates contracts and advances the revision. This helper does not itself collect approver votes or append admitted roles to `required`.

When existing terms encounter a changed roster or required-party list, `commitState` updates the terms reference and terms revision, clears a pending negotiation proposal with outcome `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`, and clears approvals when negotiation is enabled.

`requestPartyAddition` records revision-bound access requests and can emit access requests for existing parties whose access is insufficient. It validates supplied `accessDocuments` and can register them under `/partyAccess`. Stale revisions and repeated admission references are ignored. Recording or emitting these requests does not admit parties or confirm permission changes. `refreshAccessRequests` updates readiness for current-revision requests; `refresh` also initializes terms and commits activation state.

## Inherited amendment proposals

`recordAmendmentProposal` uses caller-supplied `bindings.state`, `bindings.editable`, `parameters` and `state`. It requires matching `expectedRevision`, a `path` included in `parameters.paths`, editable state exactly `true`, and a nonempty `proposalId` without `/` or `~`. It records `replacement`, the proposal revision and empty approvals, then emits `Amendment Proposed`.

An identical pending proposal returns `duplicate`; conflicting reuse or an identifier already present in history is rejected. `preservePending` defaults to `false`; when true, a different pending proposal prevents replacement.

`approveAmendmentProposal` requires the caller's channel in `parameters.approvers`. A completed identifier recorded as `true` in history returns `duplicate`; otherwise the current proposal must match and remain editable. Repeated approval by the same approver is also duplicate. New approvals return `acceptedNew`, but replacement occurs only after every configured approver has approved. Application replaces the proposed path, records completion in history, advances the amendment revision, clears the proposal and emits `Amendment Applied`.
